words.en: to hand over, to give up

units.covers: Part II, from the mother fainting to the father's return
units.en: The mother steps aside, sees the huge brown shape on the flowery wallpaper, cries 'Oh God, oh God!' and faints onto the sofa. 'You, Gregor!' shouts Grete, raising her fist – the first words she has spoken to him since his transformation. Gregor follows her into the next room to help; she jumps in fright, a medicine bottle smashes, and a splinter cuts his face. Grete shuts herself in with the mother. Full of guilt, Gregor crawls over everything until he drops onto the table. Then the father comes home. Grete tells him, 'Gregor has broken out,' and he assumes Gregor has done something violent. Gregor waits by his own door to show he'll go back in – but when his father walks in, Gregor hardly recognises him. The weak old man who used to sit around in his dressing gown has changed.

units.de: Nun aber war er doch gut aufgerichtet; in eine straffe blaue Uniform mit Goldknöpfen gekleidet, wie sie Diener der Bankinstitute tragen; über dem hohen steifen Kragen des Rockes entwickelte sich sein starkes Doppelkinn; unter den buschigen Augenbrauen drang der Blick der schwarzen Augen frisch und aufmerksam hervor; das sonst zerzauste weiße Haar war zu einer peinlich genauen, leuchtenden Scheitelfrisur niedergekämmt.
units.en: But now he was standing up straight, dressed in a tight blue uniform with gold buttons, like the ones messengers at banks wear; above the high, stiff collar of the jacket his heavy double chin spread out; under his bushy eyebrows his black eyes looked out fresh and alert; his usually messy white hair was combed down flat into a painfully exact, shiny parting.
units.explain_en: The tired father now has a job as a bank messenger – and a new energy. 'aufgerichtet' = upright. 'der Diener' usually means servant; here a messenger or porter. 'der Kragen' = collar. 'zerzaust' = messy, tousled. 'der Scheitel' = the parting in your hair. 'peinlich genau' = extremely precise ('peinlich' usually means embarrassing).

units.covers: Part II, from the father's approach to the end of Part II
units.en: With a grim face the father walks towards Gregor, who runs away from him around the room; they go round several times, slowly. Gregor soon runs out of breath. Then the father takes apples from the fruit bowl and starts throwing them. One apple hits Gregor and gets stuck in his back, causing terrible pain, and he can't move any more. As he loses consciousness, he sees his mother rush out of his room, run to the father, throw her arms around him and beg him to spare Gregor's life.

units.de: Die schwere Verwundung Gregors, an der er über einen Monat litt – der Apfel blieb, da ihn niemand zu entfernen wagte, als sichtbares Andenken im Fleische sitzen –, schien selbst den Vater daran erinnert zu haben, dass Gregor trotz seiner gegenwärtigen traurigen und ekelhaften Gestalt ein Familienglied war, das man nicht wie einen Feind behandeln durfte, sondern dem gegenüber es das Gebot der Familienpflicht war, den Widerwillen hinunterzuschlucken und zu dulden, nichts als dulden.
units.en: Gregor's serious wound, from which he suffered for more than a month – the apple stayed stuck in his flesh as a visible reminder, since nobody dared to remove it – seemed to have reminded even his father that, despite his present sad and disgusting shape, Gregor was a member of the family who must not be treated like an enemy; on the contrary, family duty demanded that they swallow their disgust and put up with him – just put up with him.
units.explain_en: Part III begins. 'leiden an' = to suffer from. 'wagen' = to dare; today people often say 'sich trauen'. 'das Andenken' = souvenir, reminder. 'ekelhaft' = disgusting. 'dulden' = to tolerate, to put up with – repeated to show how cold this 'duty' is.

words.en: to tolerate, to put up with

units.covers: Part III, from the family's tired evenings to the lodgers' dinner
units.en: In the evenings the living-room door is left open, so Gregor can watch the family from the dark. Life is quiet and exhausted: the father works as a bank messenger and sleeps in his uniform in his chair; the mother sews underwear for a shop; Grete works as a shop assistant and learns shorthand and French at night. The maid is let go, family jewellery is sold. Grete now just pushes food into Gregor's room with her foot, and the room gets filthy. A bony old cleaning woman peeks in and calls him 'old dung beetle'. The family rent a room to three strict, bearded lodgers, and all the junk ends up in Gregor's room. One evening the living-room door is left slightly open while the lodgers eat dinner.

units.de: Gerade an diesem Abend – Gregor erinnerte sich nicht, während der ganzen Zeit die Violine gehört zu haben – ertönte sie von der Küche her. Die Zimmerherren hatten schon ihr Nachtmahl beendet, der mittlere hatte eine Zeitung hervorgezogen, den zwei anderen je ein Blatt gegeben, und nun lasen sie zurückgelehnt und rauchten. Als die Violine zu spielen begann, wurden sie aufmerksam, erhoben sich und gingen auf den Fußspitzen zur Vorzimmertür, in der sie aneinandergedrängt stehen blieben.
units.en: That very evening – Gregor couldn't remember hearing the violin during the whole time – it rang out from the kitchen. The lodgers had already finished their supper; the middle one had taken out a newspaper and given the other two a page each, and now they sat leaning back, reading and smoking. When the violin began to play, they took notice, got up and went on tiptoe to the door to the hall, where they stood huddled together.
units.explain_en: The family now rents a room to three lodgers – Kafka calls them 'die Zimmerherren', an old word; today 'die Untermieter'. 'gerade an diesem Abend' = that very evening. 'ertönen' = to ring out, to sound. 'je ein Blatt' = one page each. 'auf den Fußspitzen' = on tiptoe; today 'auf Zehenspitzen'.

units.de: Man musste sie von der Küche aus gehört haben, denn der Vater rief: »Ist den Herren das Spiel vielleicht unangenehm? Es kann sofort eingestellt werden.« »Im Gegenteil«, sagte der mittlere der Herren, »möchte das Fräulein nicht zu uns hereinkommen und hier im Zimmer spielen, wo es doch viel bequemer und gemütlicher ist?« »O bitte«, rief der Vater, als sei er der Violinspieler. Die Herren traten ins Zimmer zurück und warteten. Bald kam der Vater mit dem Notenpult, die Mutter mit den Noten und die Schwester mit der Violine.
units.en: They must have been heard from the kitchen, because the father called: 'Do the gentlemen perhaps find the playing unpleasant? It can be stopped at once.' 'On the contrary,' said the middle gentleman, 'wouldn't the young lady like to come in and play here in this room, where it's so much more comfortable and cosy?' 'Oh, please!' called the father, as if he were the violinist. The gentlemen went back into the room and waited. Soon the father came with the music stand, the mother with the sheet music and the sister with the violin.
units.explain_en: The parents are painfully polite to their paying guests. 'Man musste sie gehört haben' = they must have been heard. 'einstellen' here means to stop (it can also mean to hire or to adjust). 'Im Gegenteil' = on the contrary. 'das Fräulein' = Miss, young lady – today it's old-fashioned and people avoid it. 'die Noten' = sheet music.

units.de: Die Schwester bereitete alles ruhig zum Spiele vor; die Eltern, die niemals früher Zimmer vermietet hatten und deshalb die Höflichkeit gegen die Zimmerherren übertrieben, wagten gar nicht, sich auf ihre eigenen Sessel zu setzen; der Vater lehnte an der Tür, die rechte Hand zwischen zwei Knöpfe des geschlossenen Livreerockes gesteckt; die Mutter aber erhielt von einem Herrn einen Sessel angeboten und saß, da sie den Sessel dort ließ, wohin ihn der Herr zufällig gestellt hatte, abseits in einem Winkel.
units.en: The sister calmly got everything ready to play; the parents, who had never let rooms before and so overdid their politeness towards the lodgers, didn't even dare to sit on their own chairs; the father leaned against the door, his right hand pushed between two buttons of his buttoned-up uniform coat; the mother, though, was offered a chair by one of the gentlemen and, since she left the chair where the gentleman had happened to put it, sat off to one side in a corner.
units.explain_en: 'vermieten' = to rent out; 'mieten' = to rent. 'übertreiben' = to exaggerate, to overdo. 'der Livreerock' is a servant's uniform coat – the father wears his work uniform even at home. 'zufällig' = by chance. 'der Winkel' = corner (also: angle); in everyday German 'die Ecke'.

units.de: Die Schwester begann zu spielen; Vater und Mutter verfolgten, jeder von seiner Seite, aufmerksam die Bewegungen ihrer Hände. Gregor hatte, von dem Spiele angezogen, sich ein wenig weiter vorgewagt und war schon mit dem Kopf im Wohnzimmer. Er wunderte sich kaum darüber, dass er in letzter Zeit so wenig Rücksicht auf die andern nahm; früher war diese Rücksichtnahme sein Stolz gewesen.
units.en: The sister began to play; father and mother, each from their own side, closely followed the movements of her hands. Drawn by the playing, Gregor had ventured a little further forward and already had his head in the living room. He was hardly surprised that recently he had shown so little consideration for the others; in the past this consideration had been his pride.
units.explain_en: 'sich vorwagen' = to venture forward. 'sich wundern über' = to be surprised at. 'die Rücksicht(nahme) auf' = consideration for. 'die andern' is a shortened form of 'die anderen'. 'der Stolz' = pride; 'stolz auf' = proud of.

units.de: Und dabei hätte er gerade jetzt mehr Grund gehabt, sich zu verstecken, denn infolge des Staubes, der in seinem Zimmer überall lag und bei der kleinsten Bewegung umherflog, war auch er ganz staubbedeckt; Fäden, Haare, Speiseüberreste schleppte er auf seinem Rücken und an den Seiten mit sich herum; seine Gleichgültigkeit gegen alles war viel zu groß, als dass er sich, wie früher mehrmals während des Tages, auf den Rücken gelegt und am Teppich gescheuert hätte. Und trotz dieses Zustandes hatte er keine Scheu, ein Stück auf dem makellosen Fußboden des Wohnzimmers vorzurücken.
units.en: And yet right now he would have had more reason than ever to hide: because of the dust that lay everywhere in his room and flew up at the slightest movement, he too was completely covered in dust; he dragged threads, hairs and scraps of food around with him on his back and sides; his indifference to everything was far too great for him to lie on his back and rub himself clean on the carpet, as he used to do several times a day. And despite this state he felt no shyness about moving a little way forward onto the spotless floor of the living room.
units.explain_en: 'der Grund' = reason. 'der Staub' = dust. 'die Gleichgültigkeit' = indifference ('gleichgültig' = indifferent). 'zu groß, als dass ...' = too great for ... to ... (followed by the subjunctive 'hätte'). 'makellos' = spotless, flawless. 'die Scheu' = shyness, timidity.

units.covers: Part III, from the lodgers' boredom with the music
units.en: Nobody pays attention to Gregor. The family are completely absorbed in the music. But the lodgers, who at first stood far too close behind Grete's music stand, soon drift over to the window, heads down, talking in low voices, and puff their cigar smoke up towards the ceiling. It's obvious they are disappointed and bored, and only stay out of politeness.

units.de: Und doch spielte die Schwester so schön. Ihr Gesicht war zur Seite geneigt, prüfend und traurig folgten ihre Blicke den Notenzeilen. Gregor kroch noch ein Stück vorwärts und hielt den Kopf eng an den Boden, um möglicherweise ihren Blicken begegnen zu können. War er ein Tier, da ihn Musik so ergriff? Ihm war, als zeige sich ihm der Weg zu der ersehnten unbekannten Nahrung. Er war entschlossen, bis zur Schwester vorzudringen, sie am Rock zu zupfen und ihr dadurch anzudeuten, sie möge doch mit ihrer Violine in sein Zimmer kommen, denn niemand lohnte hier das Spiel so, wie er es lohnen wollte.
units.en: And yet his sister was playing so beautifully. Her face was tilted to one side, and her eyes followed the lines of music, searching and sad. Gregor crawled forward a little more and kept his head close to the floor so that he might be able to meet her eyes. Was he an animal, if music moved him so? He felt as if the way to the unknown food he longed for was being shown to him. He was determined to push forward to his sister, tug at her skirt and so let her know that she should come into his room with her violin, because nobody here appreciated her playing the way he would.
units.explain_en: One of the most famous lines: 'War er ein Tier, da ihn Musik so ergriff?' – 'da' here means 'since, given that'. 'ergreifen' = to move deeply (also: to seize). 'ersehnt' = longed-for ('sich sehnen nach' = to long for). 'entschlossen' = determined. 'lohnen' here = to reward, to appreciate.

units.covers: Part III, from Gregor's daydream to the lodgers giving notice
units.en: Gregor dreams of keeping his sister with him in his room and telling her that he had planned to send her to the conservatory; she would cry with emotion. Then the middle lodger spots him and points: 'Mr Samsa!' The violin stops. The father tries to push the lodgers back into their room. At the door the middle lodger stamps his foot and announces that, because of the 'disgusting conditions' in this flat and family, he is leaving at once, won't pay a penny, and may even take legal action. The other two say the same and the door slams. The father sinks into his chair; the violin slides from the mother's lap with a ringing sound. Gregor, weak and disappointed, lies still and waits.

units.de: »Liebe Eltern«, sagte die Schwester und schlug zur Einleitung mit der Hand auf den Tisch, »so geht es nicht weiter. Wenn ihr das vielleicht nicht einsehet, ich sehe es ein. Ich will vor diesem Untier nicht den Namen meines Bruders aussprechen und sage daher bloß: wir müssen versuchen es loszuwerden. Wir haben das Menschenmögliche versucht, es zu pflegen und zu dulden, ich glaube, es kann uns niemand den geringsten Vorwurf machen.«
units.en: 'Dear parents,' said the sister, striking the table with her hand to begin, 'things can't go on like this. Maybe you don't see it, but I do. I won't say my brother's name in front of this monster, so all I'll say is: we must try to get rid of it. We've done everything humanly possible to look after it and put up with it; I don't think anyone can blame us in the slightest.'
units.explain_en: The turning point: Grete, who cared for Gregor most, now calls him 'es' (it). 'So geht es nicht weiter' = things can't go on like this – very common today. 'einsehet' is an old form of 'einseht' (you realise, you see). 'das Untier' = monster, beast. 'loswerden' = to get rid of. 'jemandem einen Vorwurf machen' = to blame someone.

words.en: Things can't go on like this.
to look after, to care for

units.de: »Sie hat tausendmal recht«, sagte der Vater für sich. Die Mutter, die noch immer nicht genug Atem finden konnte, fing mit einem irrsinnigen Ausdruck der Augen dumpf in die vorgehaltene Hand zu husten an. Die Schwester eilte zur Mutter und hielt ihr die Stirn. Der Vater schien durch die Worte der Schwester auf bestimmtere Gedanken gebracht zu sein, hatte sich aufrecht gesetzt, spielte mit seiner Dienermütze zwischen den Tellern, die noch vom Nachtmahl der Zimmerherren her auf dem Tische standen, und sah bisweilen auf den stillen Gregor hin.
units.en: 'She's absolutely right,' the father said to himself. The mother, who still couldn't get enough breath, began to cough hollowly into her hand, which she held in front of her mouth, with a wild look in her eyes. The sister hurried to her mother and held her forehead. The sister's words seemed to have brought the father to more definite thoughts; he had sat up straight, was playing with his messenger's cap among the plates still on the table from the lodgers' supper, and every now and then looked over at the silent Gregor.
units.explain_en: 'tausendmal recht haben' = to be completely right. 'der Atem' = breath. 'irrsinnig' = insane, crazed (today also slang for 'extremely': 'irrsinnig teuer'). 'die Stirn' = forehead. 'bisweilen' = sometimes; old-fashioned, today 'manchmal'.

units.de: »Wir müssen es loszuwerden suchen«, sagte die Schwester nun ausschließlich zum Vater, denn die Mutter hörte in ihrem Husten nichts, »es bringt euch noch beide um, ich sehe es kommen. Wenn man schon so schwer arbeiten muss, wie wir alle, kann man nicht noch zu Hause diese ewige Quälerei ertragen. Ich kann es auch nicht mehr.« Und sie brach so heftig in Weinen aus, dass ihre Tränen auf das Gesicht der Mutter niederflossen, von dem sie sie mit mechanischen Handbewegungen wischte.
units.en: 'We must try to get rid of it,' the sister now said only to her father, since her mother couldn't hear anything because of her coughing. 'It will be the death of you both, I can see it coming. When you have to work as hard as all of us do, you can't put up with this endless torment at home as well. I can't take it any more either.' And she burst into tears so violently that her tears ran down onto her mother's face, and she wiped them off with mechanical movements of her hand.
units.explain_en: 'es bringt euch noch beide um' = it will end up killing you both ('umbringen' = to kill). 'ertragen' = to bear, to stand. 'die Quälerei' = torment (from 'quälen'). 'Ich kann nicht mehr' = I can't take any more – very common. 'in Weinen/Tränen ausbrechen' = to burst into tears.

units.de: »Kind«, sagte der Vater mitleidig und mit auffallendem Verständnis, »was sollen wir aber tun?« Die Schwester zuckte nur die Achseln zum Zeichen der Ratlosigkeit, die sie nun während des Weinens im Gegensatz zu ihrer früheren Sicherheit ergriffen hatte. »Wenn er uns verstünde«, sagte der Vater halb fragend; die Schwester schüttelte aus dem Weinen heraus heftig die Hand zum Zeichen, dass daran nicht zu denken sei. »Wenn er uns verstünde«, wiederholte der Vater und nahm durch Schließen der Augen die Überzeugung der Schwester von der Unmöglichkeit dessen in sich auf, »dann wäre vielleicht ein Übereinkommen mit ihm möglich. Aber so –«
units.en: 'Child,' said the father with pity and remarkable understanding, 'but what are we to do?' The sister only shrugged her shoulders to show the helplessness that had come over her while she was crying, so unlike her earlier confidence. 'If he understood us,' said the father, half asking; the sister, still crying, shook her hand hard to show that this was out of the question. 'If he understood us,' the father repeated, closing his eyes to take in the sister's conviction that this was impossible, 'then perhaps we could come to some agreement with him. But as it is –'
units.explain_en: The father still says 'er' (he) – he hasn't quite given up on Gregor as a person. And the irony: Gregor understands every word. 'die Achseln zucken' is old; today 'mit den Schultern zucken' (to shrug). 'ratlos' = at a loss. 'Wenn er uns verstünde' = if he understood us – 'verstünde' is an older subjunctive; today 'verstehen würde'. 'daran ist nicht zu denken' = that's out of the question.

units.de: »Weg muss es«, rief die Schwester, »das ist das einzige Mittel, Vater. Du musst bloß den Gedanken loszuwerden suchen, dass es Gregor ist. Dass wir es so lange geglaubt haben, das ist ja unser eigentliches Unglück. Aber wie kann es denn Gregor sein? Wenn es Gregor wäre, er hätte längst eingesehen, dass ein Zusammenleben von Menschen mit einem solchen Tier nicht möglich ist, und wäre freiwillig fortgegangen. Wir hätten dann keinen Bruder, aber könnten weiterleben und sein Andenken in Ehren halten.
units.en: 'It has to go,' cried the sister, 'that's the only way, Father. You just have to try to get rid of the idea that it's Gregor. The fact that we believed it for so long – that's our real misfortune. But how can it be Gregor? If it were Gregor, he would have realised long ago that people can't live together with an animal like that, and he would have gone away of his own free will. Then we wouldn't have a brother, but we could go on living and honour his memory.
units.explain_en: 'Weg muss es' is emphatic word order for 'Es muss weg' (it has to go). 'das Mittel' = means, way (also: medicine). 'Wenn es Gregor wäre, er hätte ... eingesehen' = if it were Gregor, he would have realised – an unreal condition. 'freiwillig' = voluntarily. 'jemandes Andenken in Ehren halten' = to honour someone's memory.

words.en: voluntarily, of your own free will

units.de: So aber verfolgt uns dieses Tier, vertreibt die Zimmerherren, will offenbar die ganze Wohnung einnehmen und uns auf der Gasse übernachten lassen. Sieh nur, Vater«, schrie sie plötzlich auf, »er fängt schon wieder an!« Und in einem für Gregor gänzlich unverständlichen Schrecken verließ die Schwester sogar die Mutter, stieß sich förmlich von ihrem Sessel ab, als wollte sie lieber die Mutter opfern, als in Gregors Nähe bleiben, und eilte hinter den Vater, der, lediglich durch ihr Benehmen erregt, auch aufstand und die Arme wie zum Schutze der Schwester vor ihr halb erhob.
units.en: But as it is, this animal is persecuting us, driving away the lodgers, obviously wants to take over the whole flat and leave us to sleep in the street. Just look, Father,' she suddenly screamed, 'he's starting again!' And in a terror that Gregor couldn't understand at all, the sister even abandoned her mother, practically pushed herself away from her chair, as if she would rather sacrifice her mother than stay near Gregor, and rushed behind her father, who, alarmed only by her behaviour, also stood up and half raised his arms in front of her as if to protect her.
units.explain_en: Notice that Grete slips and says 'er' (he) – part of her still sees her brother. 'vertreiben' = to drive away. 'die Gasse' = lane, street (in Austria; in Germany 'die Straße'). 'opfern' = to sacrifice. 'lediglich' = merely, only (formal).

units.covers: Part III, from Gregor's slow return to the sister locking him in
units.en: Gregor hadn't meant to frighten anyone; he had only started turning round to go back to his room, which looks strange because he has to help with his head. Now everyone watches him silently and sadly. Exhausted, he slowly crawls back, and nobody hurries him. At the door he turns his head once more and sees that his mother has fallen asleep. As soon as he is inside, Grete slams the door, bolts it and turns the key, calling out 'At last!' to her parents.

units.de: »Und jetzt?« fragte sich Gregor und sah sich im Dunkeln um. Er machte bald die Entdeckung, dass er sich nun überhaupt nicht mehr rühren konnte. Er wunderte sich darüber nicht, eher kam es ihm unnatürlich vor, dass er sich bis jetzt tatsächlich mit diesen dünnen Beinchen hatte fortbewegen können. Im Übrigen fühlte er sich verhältnismäßig behaglich. Er hatte zwar Schmerzen im ganzen Leib, aber ihm war, als würden sie allmählich schwächer und schwächer und würden schließlich ganz vergehen.
units.en: 'And now?' Gregor asked himself, looking around in the dark. He soon discovered that he couldn't move at all any more. He wasn't surprised by this; if anything, it seemed unnatural to him that he had actually been able to get around on these thin little legs until now. Otherwise he felt fairly comfortable. He did have pains all over his body, but it seemed to him as if they were gradually getting weaker and weaker and would finally go away completely.
units.explain_en: Gregor's last night is told very calmly. 'die Entdeckung machen, dass ...' = to discover that ... 'sich rühren' = to move, to stir. 'sich fortbewegen' = to move about, to get around. 'Im Übrigen' = apart from that, otherwise. 'allmählich' = gradually.

units.de: Den verfaulten Apfel in seinem Rücken und die entzündete Umgebung, die ganz von weichem Staub bedeckt war, spürte er schon kaum. An seine Familie dachte er mit Rührung und Liebe zurück. Seine Meinung darüber, dass er verschwinden müsse, war womöglich noch entschiedener, als die seiner Schwester. In diesem Zustand leeren und friedlichen Nachdenkens blieb er, bis die Turmuhr die dritte Morgenstunde schlug. Den Anfang des allgemeinen Hellerwerdens draußen vor dem Fenster erlebte er noch. Dann sank sein Kopf ohne seinen Willen gänzlich nieder, und aus seinen Nüstern strömte sein letzter Atem schwach hervor.
units.en: The rotten apple in his back and the inflamed area around it, all covered in soft dust, he could hardly feel any more. He thought back on his family with tenderness and love. His own opinion that he had to disappear was, if anything, even firmer than his sister's. He stayed in this state of empty and peaceful reflection until the church clock struck three in the morning. He still saw the first light beginning to grow outside the window. Then, without his willing it, his head sank all the way down, and his last breath flowed weakly from his nostrils.
units.explain_en: Gregor dies peacefully, agreeing with his family that he must go. 'verfault' = rotten. 'entzündet' = inflamed. 'die Rührung' = emotion, tenderness. 'womöglich' here means 'if anything, perhaps even'. 'die Turmuhr' = a clock on a tower. 'die Nüstern' are an animal's nostrils – the word reminds us what Gregor has become.

units.covers: Part III, from the discovery of Gregor's body to the family's day off
units.en: Early in the morning the cleaning woman finds Gregor lying still, pokes him with her broom and then loudly tells the parents that he is dead. The family come in. 'Now we can thank God,' says Mr Samsa, and they cross themselves. Grete notices how thin he had become. It is the end of March, and the window is opened to the mild air. Mr Samsa, in his uniform and arm in arm with his wife and daughter, orders the three lodgers out of the flat, and they leave meekly. The family decide to take the day off and write letters to their employers. The cleaning woman announces, grinning, that they needn't worry about getting rid of 'the thing next door' – it has all been taken care of. Mr Samsa stops her from explaining, and she leaves, offended, slamming the door.

units.de: »Abends wird sie entlassen«, sagte Herr Samsa, bekam aber weder von seiner Frau noch von seiner Tochter eine Antwort, denn die Bedienerin schien ihre kaum gewonnene Ruhe wieder gestört zu haben. Sie erhoben sich, gingen zum Fenster und blieben dort, sich umschlungen haltend. Herr Samsa drehte sich in seinem Sessel nach ihnen um und beobachtete sie still ein Weilchen. Dann rief er: »Also kommt doch her. Lasst schon endlich die alten Sachen. Und nehmt auch ein wenig Rücksicht auf mich.« Gleich folgten ihm die Frauen, eilten zu ihm, liebkosten ihn und beendeten rasch ihre Briefe.
units.en: 'She'll be dismissed this evening,' said Mr Samsa, but he got no answer from either his wife or his daughter, because the cleaning woman seemed to have disturbed the calm they had only just found. They got up, went to the window and stayed there, holding each other. Mr Samsa turned round in his chair towards them and watched them quietly for a little while. Then he called: 'Come over here, then. Let go of the old things at last. And show me a little consideration too.' The women came to him at once, hurried over, caressed him and quickly finished their letters.
units.explain_en: The family begin to move on. 'entlassen' = to dismiss, to fire. 'die Bedienerin' is an old Austrian word for a cleaning woman; today 'die Putzfrau' or 'die Reinigungskraft'. 'sich umschlungen halten' = to hold each other tight. 'Lasst die alten Sachen' = let the past be. 'liebkosen' = to caress – old-fashioned; today 'streicheln' or 'umarmen'.

units.de: Dann verließen alle drei gemeinschaftlich die Wohnung, was sie schon seit Monaten nicht getan hatten, und fuhren mit der Elektrischen ins Freie vor die Stadt. Der Wagen, in dem sie allein saßen, war ganz von warmer Sonne durchschienen. Sie besprachen, bequem auf ihren Sitzen zurückgelehnt, die Aussichten für die Zukunft, und es fand sich, dass diese bei näherer Betrachtung durchaus nicht schlecht waren, denn aller drei Anstellungen waren, worüber sie einander eigentlich noch gar nicht ausgefragt hatten, überaus günstig und besonders für später vielversprechend.
units.en: Then all three of them left the flat together, something they hadn't done for months, and took the tram out into the open country outside the town. The carriage, in which they were the only passengers, was full of warm sunshine. Leaning back comfortably in their seats, they talked about their prospects for the future, and it turned out that on closer inspection these weren't bad at all, for all three of their jobs – which they had never really asked each other about – were very good and especially promising for later on.
units.explain_en: The final page: sunshine and hope – a shocking contrast to Gregor's dark room. 'die Elektrische' is an old word for the tram; today 'die Straßenbahn'. 'ins Freie' = out into the open air or countryside. 'die Aussichten' = prospects (also: views). 'es fand sich, dass ...' is old; today 'es stellte sich heraus, dass ...' (it turned out that ...). 'die Anstellung' = job, position.

units.de: Die größte augenblickliche Besserung der Lage musste sich natürlich leicht durch einen Wohnungswechsel ergeben; sie wollten nun eine kleinere und billigere, aber besser gelegene und überhaupt praktischere Wohnung nehmen, als es die jetzige, noch von Gregor ausgesuchte war. Während sie sich so unterhielten, fiel es Herrn und Frau Samsa im Anblick ihrer immer lebhafter werdenden Tochter fast gleichzeitig ein, wie sie in der letzten Zeit trotz aller Pflege, die ihre Wangen bleich gemacht hatte, zu einem schönen und üppigen Mädchen aufgeblüht war.
units.en: The biggest immediate improvement in their situation would of course come easily from moving; they now wanted to take a smaller and cheaper flat, but one that was better located and more practical in every way than the present one, which Gregor had chosen. While they were talking like this, it occurred to Mr and Mrs Samsa, almost at the same moment, as they looked at their daughter, who was growing livelier and livelier, how she had recently blossomed into a pretty, full-figured girl, despite all the caring that had made her cheeks pale.
units.explain_en: 'die Besserung' = improvement. 'der Wohnungswechsel' = moving flat; today 'der Umzug'. 'die jetzige' = the present one. 'einfallen' + dative = to occur to someone ('Mir fällt nichts ein' = I can't think of anything). 'die Pflege' = care, nursing – Grete's care for Gregor. 'aufblühen' = to blossom.

words.en: to occur to, to come to mind

units.de: Stiller werdend und fast unbewusst durch Blicke sich verständigend, dachten sie daran, dass es nun Zeit sein werde, auch einen braven Mann für sie zu suchen. Und es war ihnen wie eine Bestätigung ihrer neuen Träume und guten Absichten, als am Ziele ihrer Fahrt die Tochter als Erste sich erhob und ihren jungen Körper dehnte.
units.en: Growing quieter, and communicating almost unconsciously through glances, they thought that it would soon be time to find her a good husband too. And it seemed to them like a confirmation of their new dreams and good intentions when, at the end of their journey, their daughter was the first to get up and stretched her young body.
units.explain_en: The last sentence of the story: the future belongs to Grete, and Gregor is already forgotten. 'sich verständigen' = to communicate, to make yourself understood. 'brav' here means good, decent (today it mostly means 'well-behaved', about children). 'die Bestätigung' = confirmation. 'als Erste' = as the first one. 'sich dehnen' = to stretch; today usually 'sich strecken'.
